"Tighten it gently," Marcus said, not looking back. "Colony collapse disorder involves the sudden disappearance of worker bees, leaving behind the queen and immature bees. Don’t let the situation collapse by forcing the nut."

"This makes no sense," Elias muttered, though he reached into his pocket for his multi-tool. "Is the flapper wet? Should I dry it?"

"Dry it if needed," Marcus said, finally closing the door halfway. "Apis mellifera scouts perform a waggle dance to communicate the direction and distance of food sources relative to the sun. Follow the angle of the water flow, not the sound."

Elias paused, tool in hand. He looked at the closed door, then down the hall toward his own apartment. The hissing continued, relentless. He shook his head once, sharp and dismissive, and walked away.

Marcus listened until Elias’s footsteps faded. He finished his sandwich, picked up his keys, and walked out the front door, leaving the apartment silent save for the distant hum of traffic.
